note: Per-benchmark boundary error budgets (model vs annotation vs metric) would recalibrate every sub-3px progress claim; sampling design from 200 objects to benchmark-wide claims is the statistical crux. Lit-attacked below.
Inference-only longitudinal audit with a devastating potential headline ('five years of progress never reached the smallest decile'); reproduction of official numbers is the only gate.
Analytic sharpness floor validated on the model zoo makes 'losses are second-order for sharpness' a checkable claim; learned upsamplers as empirical kernels is the right pragmatic move.
The aliasing family (0003, 0154, 0165) is one paper, not three; 0003's phase-sweep causal design is the strongest instantiation - fold gap-periodicity in as a section.
Threshold-based perceptual boundary metric is the constructive complement to the C07 audits; per-use-case weights (own note) double the study size but are what makes it defensible.

Annotation-tool fingerprints are a genuinely new forensic axis with a transfer-recovery payoff; the tool-content confound needs the same-content multi-tool validation set, which nobody has - build it or drop the claim.
Occlusion-sweep information ratios are a known interpretability recipe; the size-crossover is one figure inside 0171's cleaner attribution question.

The iso-compute resolution-vs-capacity frontier is the question practitioners actually face; the shift-invariance compounding claim is the novel bit. Full grid is compute-heavy and family-replication doubles it.
Ecosystem-scale wasted-vertex accounting is a fun audit and the DP-optimal frontier is free to compute; whether human motor costs follow vertex economics (own note) decides if it means anything.
Hours-cheap, immediately actionable (one morphological parameter per class), and diagnostic of how much 'boundary error' is just bias; the residual-structure measurement doubles as the follow-up map.

Curvature-resolved error laws with architecture cutoff frequencies are good measurement science; synthetic-shape anchors solve the noisy-GT curvature problem. Competes with 0153/0174 for the same paper slot.
'The model flinches where it cannot see' is a lovely hypothesis; the texture-boundary base rate (own note) is exactly where such detectors historically die. Cheap enough to gamble on.

'Stuff-stuff boundaries are measure-zero fictions' is a sharp ontological claim with a cheap multi-annotator test and a concrete evaluation reform (band-aware scoring); the band-vs-edge classifier is the honest prerequisite.

Minimum-evaluable-object-size per dataset, derived by propagating measured annotation jitter, is a permanent public good; 'statistically vacuous SOTA claims' is the kind of finding that survives every rebuttal.
Shift-variance of CNNs is a published genre (anti-aliasing line); the small-object phase-flip quantification belongs inside 0003's phase-sweep paper, not as a third aliasing project.
Hidden cost of gradient-coupled refinement is a real hypothesis with deployment stakes (surgical/aerial lighting); isolating refinement via model surgery (own note) is fiddly and version-fragile.
Centerline+width fields exist in vessel/crack literatures; the physically-measured (caliper) downstream accuracy comparison is the genuinely new leg and requires a small collection effort.

Defocus as a per-pixel sharpness oracle exposes metrics punishing physically-inevitable uncertainty; focal-stack calibration is the right anchor. Strong section of the boundary-metric-reform agenda, mid as standalone.
Contour-spectrum fingerprinting (identify the architecture from outputs alone) is an original forensic instrument; junction-parameterization issues are real but the restricted first version is clean.

Compression-determined recall ceilings with human verification reframe 'small-object failure' as pipeline policy; codec matrix is bounded work and the deployment gap it exposes is uncomfortable and real.
'Small objects are a search problem, not a segmentation problem' is the field-redirecting claim; shares machinery with 0015 (oracle decompositions) - one strong paper exists here, not two.
Normal/tangential decomposition is a plausible metric fix with a human-validation leg; the contour-correspondence ambiguity at large errors (own note) is where the math gets contestable.

A 'machine Bouma law' - dimensionless collapse of instance-merge probability - would be the first universal capability rating for dense scenes; curve collapse either happens or it doesn't, and both outcomes teach.

The blob-prior as a measurable transfer function (with attempted inversion) upgrades folklore to instrument; competes with 0153/0161 for the same decoder-as-filter paper - pick the strongest formulation.

Physical ground truth below annotation noise opens a measurement regime segmentation has never had; ecological-validity complaint is anticipated and answered by textured/embedded variants. Flagship-quality idea.
